title: Volcanoes of Asia
intro: 10 volcanoes of Asia, one after another. Put your marker as near as you can; the nearer, the more points. The map shows coasts, rivers, lakes and borders, and you work inside this area.

rounds.name: Didicas
rounds.fact: Didicas is a compound volcano; the latest significant eruption recorded for it in the source data was in 1969. The data places it in Philippines.

rounds.name: Lower Chindwin
rounds.fact: Lower Chindwin is a volcano with a recorded summit elevation of 385 m in the source data. The data places it in Myanmar.

rounds.name: Ambalatungan Group
rounds.fact: Ambalatungan Group is a compound volcano; the latest significant eruption recorded for it in the source data was in 1952. The data places it in Philippines.

rounds.name: Dolok Sibualbuali
rounds.fact: Dolok Sibualbuali is a volcano with a recorded summit elevation of 1,819 m in the source data. The data places it in Indonesia.

rounds.name: Peuet Sague
rounds.fact: Peuet Sague is a complex volcano; the latest significant eruption recorded for it in the source data was in 1837. The data places it in Indonesia.

rounds.name: Galunggung
rounds.fact: Galunggung is a stratovolcano; the latest significant eruption recorded for it in the source data was in 1982. The data places it in Indonesia.

rounds.name: Tair, Jebel at
rounds.fact: Tair, Jebel at is a stratovolcano; the latest significant eruption recorded for it in the source data was in 2007. The data places it in Yemen.

rounds.name: Mare Island
rounds.fact: Mare Island is a volcano with a recorded summit elevation of 308 m in the source data. The data places it in Indonesia.

rounds.name: Mount Apo
rounds.fact: Mount Apo is a volcano with a recorded summit elevation of 2,954 m in the source data. The data places it in Philippines.

rounds.name: Mahawu
rounds.fact: Mahawu is a stratovolcano; the latest significant eruption recorded for it in the source data was in 1958. The data places it in Indonesia.
